Root canal therapy, or endodontic therapy, is a dental procedure that treats infected or damaged teeth. The soft tissue inside a tooth, known as the pulp, which contains blood vessels, nerves, and connective tissues, is removed during the procedure. Inflammation or infection of the pulp can occur due to decay, cracks, trauma, or repeated dental procedures, leading to severe pain and other serious health issues. To save the tooth, root canal therapy removes the infected or inflamed pulp, cleans the inside of the tooth, and fills and seals the space. This procedure is relatively painless and highly successful in saving teeth that would otherwise require extraction.
